paragraphs: Wisdom “is glorious, and never fadeth away,” and she is found by those who seek her early; the psalmist thirsts for God “in a dry and thirsty land”; Paul tells the Thessalonians not to sorrow as others who have no hope; and the wise virgins keep watch for a bridegroom who comes at midnight. The common thread is wakeful longing: the one who truly seeks God is already prepared when he comes, while the one who only waits comfortably is not.
The parable pushes the question further: what, exactly, does the prepared soul carry? Augustine asks it of the oil in the lamps, and answers:

quote.text: This, that is charity, is that way above the rest, which is with good reason signified by the oil. For oil swims above all liquids.
quote.attribution: St Augustine, Sermon 43 on the New Testament Lessons (Ben. 93), on Matthew 25:1–13, §5
quote.translation: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 6 (ed. P. Schaff)

closing: Lamps, the outward good works, are not enough; the oil is love, kept within the vessel of the heart where no one else can lend it to us. Seek Wisdom early, then, and let that seeking take the form of charity today: one patient word, one unnoticed kindness. Those who love are never caught unprepared, for the Bridegroom is already the one they are looking for.
